title: Underwriting Guide Schedule: Reinstatement Window, Interest and Evidence for Whole Life Insurance
content:
Reinstatement of a Whole Life Insurance policy that lapsed or went onto extended term or reduced paid-up insurance is measured from the default date (the lapse, extended term or reduced paid-up date). The same terms apply on every Ashgrove tier.

| Tier | Reinstatement window | Interest on back premiums (annual rate, simple) |
|---|---|---|
| Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life | 60 calendar months | 6% (0.06) |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 100 | 60 calendar months | 6% (0.06) |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 65 | 60 calendar months | 6% (0.06) |
| Ashgrove 20-Pay Whole Life | 60 calendar months | 6% (0.06) |
| Ashgrove 10-Pay Whole Life | 60 calendar months | 6% (0.06) |
| Ashgrove Single Premium Whole Life | 60 calendar months | 6% (0.06) |

## Evidence of insurability by elapsed days

The evidence required follows the calendar days from the default date to the date the reinstatement application was signed. The ladder is the same on every tier.

| Calendar days from the default date to the signed date | Evidence required |
|---|---|
| Day 0 to day 31 | None |
| Day 32 to day 180 | Statement of good health |
| Day 181 to the end of the reinstatement window | Full underwriting |

## Boundary readings (hypothetical)

- An application signed 31 days after the default date needs no evidence; one signed 32 days after needs a statement of good health.
- An application signed 180 days after the default date needs a statement of good health; one signed 181 days after needs full underwriting.
- Back premiums carry simple interest at 6% a year.
